title: OpenStax Elementary Algebra 2e, 10.1 Solve Quadratic Equations Using the Square Root Property: Solve quadratic equations of the form a x 2 = k using the Square Root Property
summary: OpenStax Elementary Algebra 2e, 10.1 Solve Quadratic Equations Using the Square Root Property: Solve quadratic equations of the form a x 2 = k using the Square Root Property
body: OpenStax Elementary Algebra 2e, section "10.1 Solve Quadratic Equations Using the Square Root Property", prints these objectives: "Solve quadratic equations of the form a x 2 = k using the Square Root Property" "Solve quadratic equations of the form a ( x − h ) 2 = k using the Square Root Property". The section text says: "Quadratic equations are equations of the form a x 2 + b x + c = 0 , where a ≠ 0 . They differ from linear equations by including a term with the variable raised to the second power. We use different methods to solve quadratic equation s than linear equations, because just adding, subtracting, multiplying, and dividing terms will not isolate the variable." This card reports that page. The objectives are the book's learning statements, not a separate proof.
